title: Diagnosing Estimator Eligibility
text: fitting estimator, iconic_diagnose() examines data reports eight ICONIC estimators eligible — , satisfy assumptions require valid. assumptions directly testable (confounder UU unobserved); diagnosis checks empirically observable projections. Diagnosis checks four things: Instrument strength. partial FF-statistic genetic instrument (G1G_1 exposure, GmG_m mediator) conventional weak-instrument threshold (F≥10F \geq 10). Negative-control validity. Three screens — A1 (NCs associate exposure), A2 (NCs independent instrument given covariates), A2’ (NCs associate outcome given exposure) — assessed via partial correlations BH-FDR control. Completeness. Whether number valid negative controls sufficient proximal estimators (PGC, PGC2, PGC2Gm), require dim⁡(Wvalid)≥k\dim(W_\text{valid}) \geq k (number latent confounders). Eligibility table. per-estimator verdict: eligible, ineligible (reason), applicable.

title: Diagnosing Estimator Eligibility
text: simulate small mediation panel genetic instrument negative controls, run diagnosis. row reports whether estimator eligible , , . example, IV2SLS requires valid exposure instrument (F≥10F \geq 10), PGC additionally requires negative-control completeness.
code: dat <- generate_toy_data(   n = 100, n_features = 5, seed = 1,   phi = 0.8, omega_1 = 0.7, omega_2 = 0.7 )  idat <- iconic_data(   X = dat$X, Y = dat$Y, M = dat$M,   G = dat$G, Gm = dat$Gm,   W1 = dat$W1, W2 = dat$W2,   covariates = dat$synthetic_data ) diag <- iconic_diagnose(idat) diag$eligibility #>   estimator eligible a2_required reason_code #> 1     UNADJ     TRUE       FALSE          OK #> 2    DIRECT     TRUE       FALSE          OK #> 3      COCA     TRUE       FALSE          OK #> 4    IV2SLS     TRUE        TRUE          OK #> 5       PGC     TRUE        TRUE          OK #> 6   IV2SLS2     TRUE        TRUE          OK #> 7      PGC2     TRUE        TRUE          OK #> 8    PGC2Gm     TRUE        TRUE          OK #>                                                                 reason #> 1                                                      always eligible #> 2                                                        G + W present #> 3                           W present, valid NCs available (A2 exempt) #> 4                                 G present (W augmentation), F_G=98.9 #> 5                      G + W present, F_G=98.9, completeness satisfied #> 6                G + Gm present (W augmentation), F_G=98.9, F_Gm=826.4 #> 7                  G + W1/W2 present, F_G=98.9, completeness satisfied #> 8 G + Gm + W1/W2 present, F_G=98.9, F_Gm=826.4, completeness satisfied

title: Diagnosing Estimator Eligibility
text: NC validity screen tests empirically observable projections three identifying assumptions negative-control feature: A1: W⟂X∣C,UW \perp X \mid C, U (NC affected exposure confounder accounted ). screen tests observable projection: association WW XX given CC. A2: W⟂G1∣C,UW \perp G_1 \mid C, U (NC instrument ). screen tests observable projection: association WW G1G_1 given CC. A2’: W⟂Gm∣C,UW \perp G_m \mid C, U (NC mediator instrument). screen tests observable projection: association WW GmG_m given CC. Features fail screen flagged, completeness count reduced accordingly. COCA estimator exempt A2 screen calibrates W∼Y+XW \sim Y + X ratio require W⟂G1W \perp G_1.

title: Genetic Instruments and Negative Controls from External Data
text: iconic identifies natural direct indirect effects (NDE/NIE) observational omics data combining genetic instruments (exposure , optionally, mediator) negative controls proxy unmeasured confounders. practice inputs come external resources: GWAS summary statistics exposure instruments, cis-eQTL scans transcriptome-wide association study (TWAS) weights mediator instruments, high-dimensional omics panels (example DNA methylation) negative-control construction. vignette demonstrates helper functions bridge external resources iconic_data object: qc_gwas_sumstats(), build_prs_ldpred2(), score_pgs_panel(), check_instrument_strength() exposure instruments; call_cis_eqtls() build_mediator_instruments() mediator instruments; beta_to_m(), residualize_matrix(), build_w_pcs(), apply_fusion_weights() negative-control panel construction; as_iconic_data() importing SummarizedExperiment directly. examples use small simulated inputs vignette builds quickly; real data calls apply unchanged.

text: build_mediator_instruments() fits elastic-net cis-prediction model per gene (via glmnet), keeps genes whose cross-validated --fold prediction passes quality gates, returns predicted mediator matrix Gm genes x samples orientation expected iconic_data(). Gene1, carries two planted cis-eQTLs, passes cross-validation gates.
code: set.seed(42) n <- 150; p <- 80 dos <- matrix(rbinom(p * n, 2, 0.3), nrow = p,               dimnames = list(paste0("1:", 1:p, ":A:G"),                               paste0("S", 1:n))) expr <- matrix(rnorm(4 * n), nrow = 4,                dimnames = list(paste0("Gene", 1:4), paste0("S", 1:n))) expr[1, ] <- expr[1, ] + 0.9 * scale(dos[5, ]) + 0.9 * scale(dos[15, ]) gp <- data.frame(gene = paste0("Gene", 1:4), chr = "1",                  tss = c(5, 25, 45, 65)) sp <- data.frame(snp = rownames(dos), chr = "1", pos = 1:p) fit <- build_mediator_instruments(expr, dos, gp, sp, seed = 1) fit$qc #>    gene n_cis_snps n_nonzero        cv_r2     cor_oof         cv_p lambda_min #> 1 Gene1         80        14  0.603994566  0.79234657 7.091717e-34  0.3699326 #> 2 Gene2         80         0 -0.016596372 -0.14033085 9.566256e-01  0.7635586 #> 3 Gene3         80        10 -0.004780502  0.07266243 1.884416e-01  0.4009905 #> 4 Gene4         80         0 -0.014790698 -0.16869659 9.804737e-01  0.5855206 #>    pass #> 1  TRUE #> 2 FALSE #> 3 FALSE #> 4 FALSE

text: Pre-computed transcriptomic weights (FUSION .wgt.RDat files, -memory list structure) can applied dosage panel build genetically predicted expression panel, can serve negative-control mediator-instrument panel.
code: dos <- matrix(rbinom(10 * 50, 2, 0.3), nrow = 10,               dimnames = list(paste0("rs", 1:10), paste0("S", 1:50))) mk_wgt <- function(snps, w) {   list(wgt.matrix = matrix(w, ncol = 1, dimnames = list(NULL, "enet")),        snps = data.frame(V2 = snps),        cv.performance = matrix(0.2, nrow = 1,                                dimnames = list("rsq", "enet"))) } wlist <- list(GeneA = mk_wgt(paste0("rs", 1:5), rep(0.1, 5)),               GeneB = mk_wgt(paste0("rs", 6:10), rep(-0.2, 5))) pos <- data.frame(ID = c("GeneA", "GeneB"), WGT = c("a.wgt.RDat", "b.wgt.RDat")) out <- apply_fusion_weights(dos, pos = pos, weights = wlist) dim(out$predicted) #> [1]  2 50

text: Even diagnosis declares estimator eligible, validity rests assumption genetic instrument exogenous — instrument-confounder correlations ρG1\rho_{G1} ρG2\rho_{G2} zero. correlations estimated data (confounders unobserved), iconic_sensitivity() sweeps plausible grid reports estimator’s bias degrades. output reports, estimator: Maximum absolute bias across sensitivity surface. Tipping points: first ρG2\rho_{G2} ρG1=0\rho_{G1} = 0 |bias|>0.10|\text{bias}| > 0.10. Texture source: whether synthetic data used generative texture model (GAN + copula) parametric benchmark generator.

title: Sensitivity Analysis and Confounding Inference
text: simulate small mediation panel, train texture model briefly, run sensitivity sweep. sensitivity-sweep chunks vignette skipped torch available. Install torch install.packages("torch") run torch::install_torch() run .
code: dat <- generate_toy_data(   n = 200, n_features = 10, seed = 1,   phi = 0.8, omega_1 = 0.7, omega_2 = 0.7 )  idat <- iconic_data(   X = dat$X, Y = dat$Y, M = dat$M,   G = dat$G, Gm = dat$Gm,   W1 = dat$W1, W2 = dat$W2,   covariates = dat$synthetic_data ) # Train a texture model briefly and attach it to the iconic_data object. input <- load_real_input_data(   X_matrix = matrix(dat$X, nrow = 1),   Y_matrix = t(dat$Y), M_matrix = t(dat$M),   W_matrix = t(dat$W), covariates_df = dat$synthetic_data )  idat$trained_gan <- train_gan_on_real_data(   input$gan_training_data,   feature_correlations = input$feature_correlations,   feature_texture = input$feature_texture,   epochs = 5, seed = 1, verbose = FALSE ) sens <- iconic_sensitivity(idat, n_iter = 3) sens

title: Sensitivity Analysis and Confounding Inference
text: infer_confounding() estimates held-fixed confounding parameters data, supplying confounding = "inferred" mode iconic_sensitivity() iconic_prospect(). inferred parameters include: Confounding strength (δ\delta): gap unadjusted OLS IV2SLS estimates. Mediator-outcome confounding (δmo\delta_{mo}): gap IV2SLS IV2SLS2 natural indirect effects. Negative-control coverage (ω1\omega_1, ω2\omega_2): R2R^2 NC feature regressed outcome residual. Number latent confounders (kk): via parallel analysis residualized outcome correlation matrix. Parameters inferred (instrument-confounder correlations ρG1\rho_{G1}, ρG2\rho_{G2}) fall back defaults warning always swept.
code: diag <- iconic_diagnose(idat) est <- iconic_estimate(idat, diagnosis = diag) conf <- infer_confounding(idat, diag, est) conf #> <iconic_confounding> #>  conf_strength    0.409 (UNADJ-IV2SLS gap (NDE)) #>  mo_confounding   0.025 (IV2SLS-IV2SLS2 NIE gap) #>  omega_1          0.485 (sqrt(R^2) of W on Y residualized on X+C) #>  warning: composite: coverage x confounder strength, not pure coverage #>  omega_2          0.484 (sqrt(R^2) of W on Y residualized on X+C) #>  warning: composite: coverage x confounder strength, not pure coverage #>  k                1 [CI: 1, 2] (parallel analysis (Horn, 1965)) #>  #>  Unavailable: rho_G1, rho_G2

title: Sensitivity Analysis and Confounding Inference
text: confounding = "default" mode uses fixed defaults (δmo=0.8\delta_{mo} = 0.8, ω1=ω2=0.7\omega_1 = \omega_2 = 0.7, ϕ=0.8\phi = 0.8) recommended starting point. confounding = "inferred" mode calibrates data uses estimator validity (e.g., IV2SLS unbiased) set benchmark whose purpose test estimator validity — inferred values read best-case calibrations stated assumptions.

title: Survival Outcomes
text: ICONIC extends estimators except COCA time--event outcomes via two-stage predictor substitution (2SPS). key insight first-stage regressions — instrumenting XX G1+W+CG_1 + W + C, instrumenting MM X̂+Gm+W+C\hat{X} + G_m + W + C, constructing bridge proxies Ŵ\hat{W} — involve continuous variables (XX, MM, WW) responses, remain ordinary least squares regardless outcome type. final outcome stage changes. (instrument-variable estimators IV2SLS / IV2SLS2, negative controls optional path-specific augmentation — W1 exposure first stage, W2 mediator outcome stages: negative controls supplied, first stages instrument genetic instrument(s) covariates alone.)

title: Survival Outcomes
text: ICONIC provides two effect scales survival outcomes: Cox log-hazard-ratio (log-HR): fits coxph(Surv(time, event) ~ X_hat + M_hat + W_hat + C) reports coefficients log-HRs. log-HR non-collapsible: conditional log-HR given covariates differs marginal log-HR even confounding, product decomposition NIE=α̂M⋅β̂M\text{NIE} = \hat{\alpha}_M \cdot \hat{\beta}_M approximate scale. log-HR scale recommended primary scale. RMST (restricted mean survival time): computes pseudo-observations via leave-one-jackknife Kaplan-Meier RMST estimate, fits OLS pseudo-observations. RMST collapsible, NDE/NIE decomposition exact scale. However, pseudo-observations introduce additional variance, producing wider confidence intervals higher RMSE Cox partial-likelihood estimator.

title: Survival Outcomes
text: COCA regresses negative control outcome (W∼Y+XW \sim Y + X) recovers τ̂=−β̂Z/β̂Y\hat{\tau} = -\hat{\beta}_Z / \hat{\beta}_Y. requires YY continuous response variable. censored time--event outcome, YY available continuous variable — outcome represented Surv(time, event) object — COCA structurally incompatible survival outcomes. ICONIC returns NA COCA survival data excludes eligibility report.

title: The Generative Texture Model
text: ICONIC uses two distinct simulation modes serve different purposes: Benchmark mode (generate_toy_data): structural data-generating process parametric Gaussian noise learned texture. ground truth (NDE, NIE, confounding strength, instrument strength) closed-form function parameters. mode used validate estimators controlled confounding scenarios exactly known ground truth. Data-calibrated mode (generative texture pipeline): trains texture model user’s data sensitivity prospective analyses calibrated realistic covariate, outcome, mediator distributions. ground truth still imposed structural skeleton, nuisance texture (marginals, correlations, covariate structure) learned data. separation deliberate: estimator validation requires transparent, reproducible data-generating process whose parameters known exactly, user-facing workflow benefits realistic data texture even cost learned noise model.

title: The Generative Texture Model
text: texture model hybrid two independently trained components, chosen match dimensionality structure target block: Sample-level GAN: MLP generator discriminator trained non-saturating BCE--logits objective, Adam optimization (β1=0.5\beta_1 = 0.5), one-sided label smoothing. GAN learns joint distribution per-sample exposure level, outcome level, mediator level, encoded covariates (one row per sample). GAN used block contains mixed continuous categorical variables whose nonlinear interactions mutual-exclusivity constraints naturally preserved flexible generator Gaussian copula. Feature-level Gaussian copula: learns full joint distribution mediator (MM) panel. feature’s marginal fit empirical CDF, parametric family (normal, log-normal, gamma, beta, selected AIC) passes Kolmogorov-Smirnov test p>0.05p > 0.05. Cross-feature dependence captured correlation matrix normal-score-transformed marginals. Neither component learns causal effect. learned texture injected structural causal model benchmark mode, drawn independently latent confounders UU open hidden backdoor. generative model never models joint (X,M,Y)(X, M, Y) learns nuisance texture, ground-truth effect guaranteed construction.

title: ICONIC: Causal Model Selection with Genetic Instruments and Negative Controls
text: iconic workbench causal inference observational omics studies unmeasured confounding biases ordinary regression. motivating application estimating causal effect exposure (e.g. gestational diabetes mellitus) panel molecular outcomes (e.g. placental transcriptome), using genetic instruments negative controls identify effect. package fits eight estimators natural direct indirect effects (NDE / NIE), diagnoses valid data, stress-tests confounding pleiotropy violations, recommends one likely unbiased. generative texture model (hybrid GAN + copula) lets sensitivity analysis mirror marginal joint structure cohort instead relying generic simulation defaults. vignette walks core workflow simulated data. statistical theory – eight estimators, negative-control assumptions (A1, A2, A2’), completeness condition, sensitivity surface, model-selection criterion – developed full accompanying manuscript technical supplement.

Stress-test robustness iconic_sensitivity(). Recommend single estimator iconic_recommend(). Prospect future studies iconic_prospect(). illustrate simulated mediation panel genetic instrument (G), exposure (X), mediator panel (M), outcome panel (Y), panel negative controls (W).

Standardize data (optionally attach a pre-trained GAN). dat <- generate_toy_data(n = 200, n_features = 10, seed = 1) idat <- iconic_data(X = dat$X, Y = dat$Y, M = dat$M,                     G = dat$G, W = dat$W, covariates = dat$synthetic_data)  # 2. title: Causal Model Selection with Genetic Instruments and Negative Controls
text: R package iconic provides model selection workflow causal inference genetic instruments negative controls observational omics data. fits eight estimators natural direct indirect effects (NDE / NIE), diagnoses valid user’s data, stress-tests confounding pleiotropy violations, recommends one likely unbiased. motivating application estimating causal effect exposure (e.g. gestational diabetes mellitus) panel molecular outcomes (e.g. placental transcriptome), package applicable observational study genetic instrument, negative controls, mediator /outcome panel. hybrid generative texture model (torch GAN sample-level structure Gaussian copula mediator panel) lets sensitivity analysis mirror marginal joint structure user’s cohort. Time--event outcomes supported Cox log-hazard-ratio restricted-mean-survival-time scales. See package vignettes quickstart guide, overview functional area, worked examples. welcome feedback questions: Email seantbresnahan3@gmail.com general questions

title: Causal Model Selection with Genetic Instruments and Negative Controls
text: iconic implements eight estimators total effect decomposition natural direct indirect effects. estimator requires different identifying assumptions; iconic_diagnose() checks met data.

title: Causal Model Selection with Genetic Instruments and Negative Controls
text: UNADJ (confounded reference): ordinary regression outcome exposure covariates. identifying assumption; biased unmeasured confounding. Serves bias reference. DIRECT: regression outcome exposure, instrument, negative controls, covariates. Uses observables remove unmeasured confounding; structurally biased. COCA (Control Outcome Calibration Approach): regresses negative controls outcome exposure, recovers effect ratio two coefficients. Efficient negative controls strong proxies confounder; unstable outcome coefficient near zero. Incompatible survival outcomes. IV2SLS (two-stage least squares): instruments exposure genetic instrument first stage, regresses outcome fitted exposure. Requires valid instrument (independent confounder, first-stage F-statistic least 10). PGC (proximal g-computation): three-stage estimator builds bridge proxy negative controls includes outcome regression. Requires negative-control completeness (enough valid controls cover latent confounders).

title: Causal Model Selection with Genetic Instruments and Negative Controls
text: estimators decompose total effect NDE (direct path) NIE (indirect path mediator) require either mediator instrument path-specific negative controls. IV2SLS2 (two-stage MR): three sequential two-stage least squares stages instrumenting exposure (exposure instrument) mediator (mediator instrument). Requires instruments valid first-stage F-statistic least 10. PGC2 (two-stage proximal mediation): builds path-specific bridge proxies path-specific negative controls — one exposure-mediator confounder one mediator-outcome confounder. Requires completeness stages. PGC2Gm (negative-control-augmented): combines first bridge mediator-instrumented mediator. Requires path-specific negative controls mediator instrument; residual bias confounder-correlated mediator instrument smaller IV2SLS2 nonzero.

title: Causal Model Selection with Genetic Instruments and Negative Controls

Benchmark simulation mode: structural synthetic-data generator (generate_toy_data). Two latent confounders drawn independently — one opening backdoor path exposure mediator, opening backdoor path mediator outcome. exposure, mediator, outcome generated structural causal model parametric Gaussian noise every stage. Genetic instruments exposure mediator drawn standard normal, path-specific negative controls generated coverage-weighted functions confounders plus noise. ground-truth quantities fixed, tunable parameters.

Neither component learns causal effect; ground truth imposed structural skeleton guaranteed construction. Data-calibrated simulation mode: hybrid GAN-plus-copula generative texture pipeline. (1) Texture learning: sample-level GAN feature-level Gaussian copula trained independently user’s data. (2) Structural skeleton: learned texture injected structural causal model, drawn independently latent confounders. title: Causal Model Selection with Genetic Instruments and Negative Controls
code: library(iconic) set.seed(1)  # Simulated mediation panel: exposure X, mediator M, outcome Y, # genetic instrument G, negative controls W. dat <- generate_toy_data(n = 200, n_features = 10, seed = 1) idat <- iconic_data(   X = dat$X, Y = dat$Y, M = dat$M,   G = dat$G, W = dat$W, covariates = dat$synthetic_data )  # 1. Diagnose which estimators are eligible. diag <- iconic_diagnose(idat)  # 2. Estimate NDE/NIE with all eligible estimators. est <- iconic_estimate(idat)  # 3. Train a texture model once and attach it (reused downstream). input <- load_real_input_data(   X_matrix = matrix(dat$X, nrow = 1), Y_matrix = t(dat$Y),   M_matrix = t(dat$M), W_matrix = t(dat$W),   covariates_df = dat$synthetic_data ) idat$trained_gan <- train_gan_on_real_data(   input$gan_training_data,   feature_correlations = input$feature_correlations,   feature_texture = input$feature_texture,   epochs = 100, seed = 1 )  # 4. Stress-test robustness (reuses the attached GAN). sens <- iconic_sensitivity(idat, confounding = "inferred")  # 5. Recommend a single estimator. rec <- iconic_recommend(idat, diag, est, sens)  # 6. Prospect for future studies (reuses the attached GAN). pros <- iconic_prospect(idat, confounding = "inferred")

title: Apply FUSION/TWAS eQTL weights to a dosage matrix — apply_fusion_weights
code: # Simulate two FUSION-style weight objects in memory dos <- matrix(rbinom(10 * 50, 2, 0.3), nrow = 10,               dimnames = list(paste0("rs", 1:10), paste0("S", 1:50))) mk_wgt <- function(snps, w) {   list(wgt.matrix = matrix(w, ncol = 1, dimnames = list(NULL, "enet")),        snps = data.frame(V2 = snps),        cv.performance = matrix(0.2, nrow = 1,                                dimnames = list("rsq", "enet"))) } wlist <- list(GeneA = mk_wgt(paste0("rs", 1:5), rep(0.1, 5)),               GeneB = mk_wgt(paste0("rs", 6:10), rep(-0.2, 5))) pos <- data.frame(ID = c("GeneA", "GeneB"), WGT = c("a.wgt.RDat", "b.wgt.RDat")) out <- apply_fusion_weights(dos, pos = pos, weights = wlist) dim(out$predicted) #> [1]  2 50

title: Build an exposure polygenic score with LDpred2-auto — build_prs_ldpred2
text: sumstats data.frame GWAS summary statistics, ideally pre-processed qc_gwas_sumstats(). Must contain (standardization) chr, pos, a0, a1, beta, beta_se, n_eff; freq used SD-ratio QC present. ld_ref Either path bigsnpr .rds backing file (bigsnpr::snp_readBed()) attached bigSNP object. match ancestry GWAS. genotypes Optional: path bigsnpr .rds attached bigSNP object target cohort scored. NULL (default), LDpred2 effect sizes returned. hapmap3 Optional character vector variant IDs (rsIDs chr:pos:a0:a1 keys) restrict analysis (e.g. HapMap3). Restriction improves chain stability; NULL (default) uses matched variants. max_variants Optional integer: matched variant count exceeds , systematically thin approximately max_variants variants (evenly spaced along genome) computing LD. Default NULL (thinning). Use e.g. 250000 bound memory. n_chains Integer: number LDpred2-auto chains. Default 30. p_range Numeric length-2: range initial per-chain proportion--causal-variants grid, log-spaced. Default c(1e-4, 0.2). burn_in Integer: burn-iterations per chain. Default 500. num_iter Integer: sampling iterations per chain (burn-). Default 500. shrink_corr Numeric: LD shrinkage parameter. Default 0.95; reduce ~0.4 SD-ratio QC flags >10% variants. allow_jump_sign Logical: allow sign jumps across chains. Default FALSE (recommended auto mode). use_mle Logical: use MLE hyperparameter updates. Default FALSE (appropriate moderate GWAS sample sizes). chain_filter_quantile Numeric: chains kept range posterior corr_est exceeds chain_filter_quantile-quantile chain ranges times 0.95. Default 0.95. impute_mean Logical: mean-impute missing target genotypes scoring. Default TRUE. ncores Integer: threads bigsnpr. Default 1. verbose Logical: print progress. Default TRUE.

Strategy (three stages): Bridge X (purge conf_XM X): X_resid = residuals(X ~ G1 + C); W_hat_X = bridge(X_resid ~ W1) (fitted values, proxy conf_XM); X_hat = fitted(X ~ G1 + W_hat_X + C). Weak-IV check: partial F G1 >= min_f. Bridge M (purge conf_MY M): M_resid = residuals(M ~ X_hat + C) (gm = NULL), M_resid = residuals(M ~ Gm + C) (gm supplied); W_hat_M = bridge(M_resid ~ W2) (fitted values, proxy conf_MY); M_hat = fitted(M ~ X_hat + W_hat_M + C) (gm = NULL), M_hat = fitted(M ~ X_hat + Gm + W_hat_M + C) (gm supplied); alpha_M = coefficient X_hat. Outcome: Y ~ X_hat + M_hat + W_hat_X + W_hat_M + C; NDE = coefficient X_hat, beta_M = coefficient M_hat. NIE = alpha_M * beta_M (delta-method SE). key advantage fit_iv2sls_mediation2: PGC-2 require instrument exogeneity. mediator instrument Gm correlated confounder conf_MY (rho_G2 > 0), IV2SLS2 biased PGC-2's bridge absorbs conf_MY regardless instrument violation. tipping-point simulation maps PGC-2 bias crosses IV2SLS2 bias.

text: n Sample size. Default 500. n_features Number outcome negative-control features. Default 20. n_mediators Number independent mediators. > 1, mediator M_m genetic instrument Gm_m contributes additively Y. M Gm returned n_mediators x n matrices. Default 1 (single mediator, backward compatible). beta_X Direct effect X Y (true NDE). Default 0.10. alpha_M Effect X mediator M. Default 0.50. beta_M Effect M Y (per-mediator NIE = alpha_M * beta_M; total NIE = n_mediators * alpha_M * beta_M). Default 0.30. conf_str Confounding strength delta. Default 0.80. w_signal Proxy quality omega (0 = noise, 1 = perfect U proxy). Default 0.70. mo_confounding Strength U1 -> M (mediator-outcome confounding). 0 = M-O confounding (original DGP). Default 0. pleio Strength direct G -> Y path (horizontal pleiotropy), violating exclusion restriction. 0 = pleiotropy (valid instrument, original DGP). Default 0. phi Strength mediator instrument Gm -> M. 0 = mediator instrument (original DGP, Gm generated). NULL = use w_signal. feat_cor Within-module feature correlation. > 0, idiosyncratic noise Y W panels drawn multivariate normal block-diagonal correlation matrix modelling co-expression modules. 0 = independent noise (backward compatible). Default 0. Sensitivity sweeps ICONIC preprint show estimator performance largely insensitive feat_cor, retained completeness rather primary stress axis. separate_U Defunct. Passing value errors message pointing replacement per-path loading vectors lambda_XM / lambda_MY. what: iconic: Causal Model Selection with Genetic Instruments and Negative Controls — iconic-package
title: iconic: Causal Model Selection with Genetic Instruments and Negative Controls — iconic-package
text: Provides model selection workflow causal inference genetic instruments negative controls observational omics data. package fits eight estimators natural direct indirect effects (NDE/NIE), diagnoses valid user's data via instrument-strength checks negative-control validity screens (A1, A2, A2'), stress-tests confounding pleiotropy violations, recommends estimator likely unbiased. hybrid generative texture model (torch GAN sample-level structure Gaussian copula mediator panel) lets sensitivity analysis mirror marginal joint structure user's cohort. modular API comprises iconic_data() standardize data, iconic_diagnose() assess estimator eligibility, iconic_estimate() fit eligible estimators, iconic_sensitivity() sweep instrument exogeneity, iconic_recommend() rank estimators identification strength robustness, iconic_prospect() plan future studies. infer_confounding() estimates held-fixed confounding parameters data. Helper functions construct exposure instruments (polygenic scores GWAS summary statistics PGS Catalog scoring files), mediator instruments (cis-eQTL scans elastic-net predicted-expression composites), negative-control panels (principal components residualized omics matrices), data can imported directly SummarizedExperiment objects. Time--event outcomes supported Cox log-hazard-ratio restricted-mean-survival-time scales. torch package required generative texture model (sensitivity prospective analysis); functionality works without .

title: Diagnose data and determine estimator eligibility — iconic_diagnose
text: Instrument strength: first-stage partial F-statistics G (exposure instrument) Gm (mediator instrument), Stock-Yogo weak-instrument threshold (F >= 10). NC validity (A1): screens negative-control feature association exposure X (empirically testable projection "W independent X given C, U"; nc_validity_screen()). NC independence (A2): screens NC association instrument G (empirically testable projection "W independent G given C, U"; nc_independence_check()). NC independence (A2'): screens NC association mediator instrument Gm (empirically testable projection "W independent G_m given C, U"; nc_independence_check_gm()). Path completeness: checks whether valid NC panel enough features span confounder subspace captures confounder covariance (nc_completeness_check()).

title: Fit all eligible estimators on real data — iconic_estimate
text: data iconic_data object iconic_data(). methods Optional character vector estimator names run (e.g. c("IV2SLS", "PGC")). Default NULL: run eligible. diagnosis Optional iconic_diagnosis object iconic_diagnose(). supplied, eligible estimators run (unless methods run_all overrides). alpha Significance threshold significance flags. Default 0.05. n_cores Number parallel workers per-feature (per-mediator) estimation. Default 1 (sequential). Uses parallel::mclapply Unix PSOCK cluster Windows. min_f Minimum partial F per-transcript weak-instrument gate inside IV2SLS, IV2SLS2, PGC2Gm. Default NULL: inherits diagnosis$min_f diagnosis supplied, otherwise 10. Pass explicit value override. run_all Logical. Default FALSE. TRUE, overrides diagnosis-based eligibility runs every method whose required data exists (via .auto_eligible_methods()). per-transcript min_f gate still applies. "force run" escape hatch exploratory analysis. se_method Character: "delta" (default), "bootstrap", "composite". "bootstrap", mediation NDE_se/NIE_se replaced SD n_boot nonparametric bootstrap resamples. "composite", mediation NIE_p replaced Huang (2019) JT-comp composite null p-value, accounts three-case structure H0: alpha*beta=0 provides higher power Sobel/Wald test signals sparse. applies mediation mode. NDE_p NIE_se unchanged. n_boot Integer: number bootstrap resamples se_method = "bootstrap". Default 500. effect_scale Character: "loghr" (default) "rmst". used data$outcome_type = "survival". "loghr" fits Cox proportional-hazards models reports log-hazard ratios. "rmst" regresses leave-one-RMST pseudo-observations (Graw et al. 2009) via OLS, reporting effects restricted-mean-survival-time (time) scale — collapsible alternative NDE/NIE product decomposition exact. Ignored (message) outcome_type = "continuous". tau Numeric: RMST restriction time horizon. Default NULL (90th percentile follow-). Used effect_scale = "rmst".

title: Load and standardise a real multi-omic dataset for GAN training — load_real_input_data
text: X_matrix Exposure panel, features x samples (e.g. exposure molecular score across probes). Column means become per-sample exposure. Y_matrix Outcome, either scalar vector length n_samples (e.g. clinical molecular trait) features x samples matrix. vector, defines n_samples; matrix, n_samples n_features. M_matrix Mediator panel, features x samples (e.g. gene transcript expression). supplied, per-sample summary added GAN training frame (generator learns mediator's marginal distribution) residual correlation matrix computed stored. W_matrix Optional negative-control panel, features x samples. supplied controls treated user-provided real structure; NULL generated negative-control model simulation time. covariates_df Optional data frame sample-level covariates. sample_id column used align samples present; recognised columns sex, GA, mother_ethnicity encoded, numeric columns z-scored kept. Names colliding estimator-reserved tokens renamed cov_ prefix. example Force return built-example dataset. Default FALSE (auto-enabled matrices given). marginal_method Marginal fitting method feature-level copula texture model (mediator panel): "auto" (default, uses parametric KS test passes p > 0.05, otherwise empirical), "empirical" (always empirical CDF), "parametric" (always best parametric fit AIC). See train_feature_texture(). residualize_on Character: "XC" (default) residualizes Y/W correlation exposure + covariates ; "XCW" additionally residualizes W bridge proxy (PC1 W), reducing U-signature double-counting. Recommended completeness-capture test reports "strong". Z_matrix Defunct. Renamed X_matrix; passing value errors message pointing X_matrix. Retained signature catch redirect old calls.

title: Check negative-control completeness (dimensional + covariance-capture) — nc_completeness_check
text: (1) Dimensional (legacy count-based check): number valid negative-control features vs number latent confounders k. Bridge-function estimators (COCA, PGC) require least many valid controls confounders (Miao, Geng & Tchetgen Tchetgen, 2018). dim(W_valid) < k, estimator built controls can recover causal effect, regardless sample size. (2) Covariance-capture: whether controls actually capture confounder covariance — .e., whether adding W reduces U's contribution outcome toward zero, operationalized incremental R^2 W outcome covariates alone, permutation null. addresses concern completeness covariance captured, proxy number. composite completeness verdict requires dimensional component pass (satisfied/borderline) capture component non- negligible (strong/weak). dimensional component passes capture negligible, verdict "weak-capture".

title: Screen negative controls for exposure dependence (W | X | C) — nc_validity_screen

Distinguishing "W downstream X" (true A1 violation) "W shares cause X" (intended NC behavior) remains open problem without clean test statistic. relative_effect column (|partial_r(W,X|C)| / |partial_r(W,U_proxy|C)|, u_proxy supplied) exposed diagnostic: control downstream X tends larger W-X association relative W-U association, separation always clean. Analysts inspect partial_r relative_effect together rather relying single gate.

what: Standardize and QC GWAS summary statistics — qc_gwas_sumstats
title: Standardize and QC GWAS summary statistics — qc_gwas_sumstats
text: Renames common GWAS summary-statistic column conventions bigsnpr convention (chr, pos, a0, a1, beta, beta_se, n_eff, freq) applies standard LDpred2 QC filters: missing/invalid values, extreme effect sizes, ambiguous-strand (/T C/G) SNPs, — effect allele frequencies available — standard-deviation ratio check LDpred2 tutorial.

title: Standardize and QC GWAS summary statistics — qc_gwas_sumstats
code: qc_gwas_sumstats(   sumstats,   n_eff = NULL,   drop_ambiguous = TRUE,   beta_iqr_mult = 10,   sd_ratio_range = c(0.5, 2),   sd_y = NULL )

title: Standardize and QC GWAS summary statistics — qc_gwas_sumstats
text: sumstats data.frame GWAS summary statistics. Recognized column aliases: chr/chromosome/CHR; pos/base_pair_location/ BP; a1/effect_allele/ALT; a0/other_allele/REF; beta/BETA/effect/logOR; beta_se/standard_error/se/SE; freq/effect_allele_frequency/EAF/FRQ; n_eff/n/N; p/p_value/P; rsid/rs_id/SNP/ID. n_eff Optional scalar: effective sample size, used input sample-size column. drop_ambiguous Logical: drop /T C/G SNPs whose strand resolved. Default TRUE. beta_iqr_mult Numeric: drop SNPs \(|\beta - \mathrm{median}(\beta)| >\) beta_iqr_mult \(\times \mathrm{IQR}(\beta)\). Default 10. Set Inf skip. sd_ratio_range Numeric length-2: acceptable range ratio summary-statistic-implied genotype SD frequency-implied SD, \(\sqrt{2 f (1-f)}\). SNPs outside range dropped. Default c(0.5, 2) (LDpred2 tutorial). Requires freq; skipped message frequencies absent. sd_y Optional scalar: phenotypic SD used SD-ratio check. NULL (default), estimated 1st percentile \(\sqrt{0.5 (n_{eff} \cdot se^2 + \beta^2)}\) across SNPs, continuous-trait approximation used LDpred2 tutorial.

title: Standardize and QC GWAS summary statistics — qc_gwas_sumstats
text: list : sumstats data.frame QC-passing variants standardized columns chr, pos, a0, a1, beta, beta_se, (available) n_eff, freq, p, rsid. qc data.frame counts input variants variants dropped filter. sd_ratio numeric vector SD ratios retained variants, NULL check skipped.

title: Standardize and QC GWAS summary statistics — qc_gwas_sumstats

title: Residualize a feature matrix on covariates — residualize_matrix

title: Residualize a feature matrix on covariates — residualize_matrix

Default 0. rho_G1 Correlation G1 conf_XM. Default 0. rho_G2 Correlation G2 conf_MY. Default 0. rho_pop Shared population structure. title: Generate one synthetic dataset under the generalised SCM — run_single_iteration
text: trained_gan Optional iconic_gan train_gan_on_real_data(), supplying realistic covariate/outcome texture. NULL, default synthetic covariates used. n_synthetic_samples Sample size. Default 500. n_features Number outcome (control) features. Default 20. n_confounders Number latent confounders k. Default 1 (backward-compatible single-confounder model). n_mediators Number independent mediators. > 1, mediator genetic instrument Gm contributes additively Y. Default 1 (single mediator, backward compatible). beta_X Direct effect X Y (true NDE). Default 0.10. alpha_M Effect X mediator M. Default 0.50. beta_M Effect M Y. Default 0.30. effect_size Optional shortcut: non-NULL, sets pure direct total effect (beta_X = effect_size, alpha_M = beta_M = 0). Use 0 null (Type error) simulations. Default NULL (use mediation parameters). conf_strength Overall confounding strength (analogue conf_str); scales confounder loadings X Y. Default 0.80. coverage well negative controls span confounder subspace, [0, 1] (passed nc_model). Default 1. captured Integer indices confounders negative controls see (passed nc_model). Default k. nc_model Negative-control model: function (U, covariates, params) -> W, registered name ("proxy", "cpg"). Default `"proxy". nc_params Extra named parameters forwarded nc_model. mo_confounding Strength U1 -> M (mediator-outcome confounding). 0 = M-O confounding (original DGP). Default 0. > 0, first confounder U[,1] also affects M, creating M-O confounding mediation estimators benchmarked . pleio Strength direct G -> Y path (horizontal pleiotropy), violating exclusion restriction. 0 = pleiotropy (valid instrument, original DGP). Default 0. > 0, G affects Y directly addition X, allowing benchmarking IV/2SLS instrument invalidity. phi Strength mediator instrument Gm -> M. 0 = mediator instrument (original DGP, Gm generated). Default 0. > 0, valid instrument M generated (independent U G, direct path Y), enabling point identification NDE/NIE via fit_iv2sls_mediation2() even M-O confounding. gamma_G Strength exposure instrument G -> X. Default 0.6. rho_G1 Correlation G1 conf_XM (instrument exogeneity violation). Default 0. rho_G2 Correlation G2 conf_MY (instrument exogeneity violation). Default 0. rho_pop Shared population structure inducing G1-G2 correlation Default 0. lambda_XM Optional length-k loading vector giving confounder's weight X->M backdoor path. NULL (default) = shared loadings. lambda_MY Optional length-k loading vector giving confounder's weight M->Y backdoor path. NULL (default) = shared loadings. omega_1 Coverage conf_XM W1. NULL = use coverage. omega_2 Coverage conf_MY W2. NULL = use coverage. feat_cor Within-module feature correlation. > 0 GAN provide feature_correlations, block-diagonal correlation matrix used NC outcome noise. GAN-learned correlations take precedence. Default 0. separate_U Defunct. Passing value errors message pointing replacement per-path loading vectors lambda_XM / lambda_MY. Retained signature catch redirect old calls. u_strength Numeric vector: per-confounder strength profile (length k). Default NULL → rep(1, k) (equal strength, backward compatible). Recycled length k normalized total confounding budget unchanged. w_coverage_profile list optional w1 w2 numeric vectors: per-control coverage conf_XM / conf_MY (length n_features). Default NULL → scalar omega applied uniformly. MMExp, MMOut, MMCon, MMCpG Per-pathway confounding multipliers (exposure, outcome, controls, methylation). Default 1. outcome_type "continuous" (default) "survival" "survival", linear predictor converted surv_time surv_event via exponential PH model. surv_h0 Baseline hazard survival DGP. Default 0.1. surv_event_frac Target fraction observed events. Default 0.6. surv_censor_rate Explicit censoring rate. Default NULL. seed Optional RNG seed.

text: dat_or_params dat list generate_toy_data() named list DGP parameters. conf_grid Swept values conf_str (confounding strength). title: Scenario manifest: truth and parameter ranges for a simulation — scenario_manifest
text: named list elements: estimands Named numeric vector: NDE, NIE, total. modifiable_parameters Data frame columns parameter, value, swept_range. value scalar used (NA grid supplied); swept_range comma-separated string grid values, NA parameter held fixed. fixed_parameters Data frame columns parameter, value.

title: Scenario manifest: truth and parameter ranges for a simulation — scenario_manifest
text: dat_or_params may either: list returned generate_toy_data(), case estimands fixed parameters read object (true_NDE, true_NIE, true_total, n, n_features, n_mediators, lambda_XM, lambda_MY, feat_cor); bare named list DGP parameters (beta_X, alpha_M, beta_M, n_mediators, n, n_features, lambda_XM, lambda_MY, feat_cor, ...), case estimands recomputed NDE = beta_X, NIE = n_mediators * alpha_M * beta_M, total = NDE + NIE. *_grid arguments record swept ranges modifiable parameters. grid argument omitted NULL, corresponding modifiable parameter reported scalar value (range).

what: Score a published polygenic-score panel on a dosage matrix — score_pgs_panel
title: Score a published polygenic-score panel on a dosage matrix — score_pgs_panel
text: Applies published set per-variant weights (e.g. PGS Catalog scoring file, already LD-aware) directly genotype dosage matrix. Matching chr:pos:ref:alt key (automatic allele-flip handling: genotype stores opposite orientation, weight negated) rsID present.

title: Score a published polygenic-score panel on a dosage matrix — score_pgs_panel
code: score_pgs_panel(weights, genotypes, impute_mean = TRUE, scale_score = TRUE)

title: Score a published polygenic-score panel on a dosage matrix — score_pgs_panel
text: weights data.frame variant weights. Recognized columns: chr/chr_name, pos/chr_position, a1/effect_allele, a0/other_allele, weight/effect_weight, optionally rsid. PGS Catalog scoring files can read directly utils::read.delim() (skip header comment lines). genotypes numeric dosage matrix (variants x samples, dosages 0-2) whose rownames either chr:pos:ref:alt keys rsIDs matching weights. bigsnpr::snp_attach() bigSNP object also accepted (requires bigsnpr). impute_mean Logical: mean-impute missing dosages per variant. Default TRUE. scale_score Logical: scale resulting score mean 0 / sd 1. Default TRUE.

title: Score a published polygenic-score panel on a dosage matrix — score_pgs_panel
text: list : score named numeric vector per-sample scores. matched data.frame matched variants weights used (flip correction). n_input number weight-panel variants.

title: Score a published polygenic-score panel on a dosage matrix — score_pgs_panel
code: # Toy dosage matrix: 4 variants x 50 samples dos <- matrix(rbinom(4 * 50, 2, 0.3), nrow = 4,               dimnames = list(c("1:100:A:G", "1:200:C:T",                                 "1:300:G:A", "2:400:T:C"),                               paste0("S", 1:50))) wts <- data.frame(chr = c(1, 1, 2), pos = c(100, 300, 400),                   a1 = c("A", "G", "T"), a0 = c("G", "A", "C"),                   weight = c(0.1, -0.2, 0.05)) out <- score_pgs_panel(wts, dos) plot(out$score)

text: release addresses coauthor (JYH) comments proximal-completeness condition, negative-control validity screens, recommendation criterion, simulation reporting. changes backward-compatible (new arguments carry defaults preserving v0.9.1 behavior).

title: iconic 0.9.2
text: Covariance-capture completeness test (nc_completeness_capture()): operationalizes proximal completeness condition whether negative-control panel captures confounder covariance (incremental R^2 W outcome, permutation null), rather proxy count. nc_completeness_check() now returns dimensional verdict (dim(W_valid) vs k) capture verdict, plus composite. Addresses JYH comments completeness covariance captured, proxy number. Magnitude-based A1 screen: nc_validity_screen() gains criterion = c("fdr", "magnitude", "") argument magnitude_threshold (default 0.10). magnitude branch flags controls partial-correlation size, significance, addressing concern FDR hypothesis tests underpowered “always significant via U.” Returns per-branch verdicts (verdict_fdr, verdict_magnitude). COCA A2 exemption: COCA longer requires A2 (instrument- independence) screen eligibility, A1 + completeness. A2 remains required IV2SLS, PGC, IV2SLS2, PGC2, PGC2Gm. eligibility table gains a2_required column. Per-scenario recommendations: iconic_recommend() now returns $per_scenario table (top estimator per sensitivity-surface cell) addition global recommendation, criterion argument ("minimax_bias", "ci_coverage", "combined"). sensitivity surface gains NDE_coverage NIE_coverage columns (Wald CI coverage delta-method SE). Tier-label changed “identified stated assumptions.” CI coverage, %bias, mean SE benchmarks: simulation summarization now reports NDE_coverage, NIE_coverage, NDE_pct_bias, NIE_pct_bias, NDE_mean_se, NIE_mean_se. mediation estimators iconic_estimate() gain se_method = c("delta", "bootstrap") (default "delta") n_boot (default 500) optional bootstrap SE. Scenario manifest: new scenario_manifest() helper exposes ground-truth estimands swept vs. fixed parameter ranges; iconic_sensitivity() gan_mediation_sensitivity() add $manifest field return value. U/W strength heterogeneity: generate_toy_data() run_single_iteration() gain u_strength (per-confounder scaling) w_coverage_profile (per-control coverage) arguments, allowing confounders/proxies stronger others. Exposed returned dataset. Optional U-deconfounding residual correlation: .residual_correlation() texture-training entry points gain residualize_on = c("ZC", "ZCW") (default "ZC"). "ZCW", residual correlation partials U-signature captured W, reducing double-counting U’s cross-feature signature. $double_count_estimate diagnostic exposed. Defaults enumeration allow_no_proxy: infer_confounding(), iconic_sensitivity(), iconic_prospect() documentation gains @section Defaults block. iconic_prospect() iconic_diagnose() gain allow_no_proxy (default TRUE): FALSE, error IV NC supplied.

title: iconic 0.9.1
text: Panel-level instrument-strength distributions: .check_instrument_strength() now computes partial F every mediator panel (just first transcript) G Gm. full distributions exposed diag[["instrument_strength"]][["F_G"]] diag[["instrument_strength"]][["F_Gm"]] (numeric vectors, one entry per instrument/mediator). iconic_diagnose() gains g_threshold = list(E, R) gm_threshold = list(E, R) arguments: instrument-dependent method eligible least E fraction transcripts F >= R. Default NULL preserves legacy scalar behavior (median F vs min_f). run_all flag: iconic_estimate() gains run_all = FALSE min_f arguments. run_all = TRUE overrides diagnosis eligibility, running every method whose required data exists. min_f (default NULL) inherited diagnosis$min_f diagnosis supplied explicitly set, otherwise defaults 10. passed per-transcript weak-instrument gate (previously hardcoded 10 inside estimator functions never configurable top-level API).

title: iconic 0.9.1
text: Parallel progress reporting: .parallel_lapply() now reports percentage-complete progress parallel execution (Unix mclapply Windows PSOCK), just start message. Tasks split ~10 chunks; progress message printed chunk completes. Previously, parallel runs printed single start line produced intermediate output completion. Sequential timing bug: final “100%” completion line sequential mode now reports total elapsed time task start, just elapsed time since last 30-second update. separate start_time retained alongside throttle timer. Unified progress cadence: sequential parallel paths now report ~10% increments, replacing previous 30-second throttle sequential mode. Progress messages include cumulative percentage, task count, elapsed seconds.

title: iconic 0.9.0
text: Hybrid GAN + copula texture model: generative texture model now hybrid two independently trained components. sample-level torch GAN learns joint distribution per-sample exposure, outcome, mediator level, encoded covariates. new feature-level Gaussian copula model (train_feature_texture() / sample_feature_texture()) learns full joint distribution mediator (M) panel — marginal distributions cross-feature dependence — directly user’s data. Gaussian copula mediator panel: mediator feature’s marginal fitted empirical CDF default, parametric fallback (normal, log-normal, gamma, beta, selected AIC) used parametric fit passes Kolmogorov-Smirnov goodness--fit test p > 0.05. user may override automatic selection via marginal_method parameter (“auto”, “empirical”, “parametric”). Cross-feature dependence captured Gaussian copula correlation matrix normal-transformed scores. simulation, copula draws replace parametric Gaussian noise mediator structural equations, preserving realistic marginal shapes correlations user’s cohort maintaining closed-form ground truth. torch now hard dependency: MVN fallback removed entirely. torch moved Suggests Imports. GAN component requires torch; train_gan_on_real_data() errors torch unavailable. W panel unchanged: negative-control (W) panel continues use pluggable nc_model residual correlation matrices. copula replaces residual correlation approach mediator panel.

title: iconic 0.8.4
text: Full negative-control panel estimators: DIRECT, IV2SLS, IV2SLS2 now use full W panel (q negative-control features) regression formulas, rather matching single NC feature outcome feature. improves confounding adjustment aligns code model specification described manuscript. new internal .expand_w() helper handles vector matrix W inputs. COCA continues use rowMeans(W) scalar summary (required ratio-estimator form). PGC PGC2 already used full panel via bridge regressions. Per-mediator genetic instruments: generate_toy_data() run_single_iteration() now accept n_mediators parameter (default 1, backward compatible). n_mediators > 1, mediator M_m independent genetic instrument Gm_m, M Gm returned n_mediators x n matrices. mediation estimation pipeline estimates mediator one time (M_vec = M[m, ]), mirroring iconic_estimate() behavior. run_mediation_sim() sweep_mediation_param() also accept n_mediators. Vignette migration: walkthrough document moved package root vignettes/iconic-walkthrough.Rmd proper VignetteIndexEntry knitr::rmarkdown engine. output format now rmarkdown::html_vignette. VignetteBuilder: knitr added DESCRIPTION; knitr rmarkdown added Suggests.
